title: Use components as filing drawers
summary: Learn the recurring pieces of a character to file it in memory, without trusting them as meaning.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: Most characters you meet are built from a small set of recurring pieces, so name the pieces you see again and again and the count of things you must memorise drops sharply. A piece on the left often hints at a category: the water mark sits on the left of 洗 xǐ (to wash), 海 hǎi (sea), and 河 hé (river); the speech mark sits on the left of 说 shuō (to speak), 话 huà (words), and 请 qǐng (please). Treat that as a filing drawer, not a definition, because centuries of trimming have left many pieces purely phonetic. When a character will not stick, break it into two or three parts and say each part aloud; the shape becomes a story instead of a pile of lines.
